tip.sweetness: Sweetness comes from 'Residual Sugar' (g/L). WSET classifies it from Bone Dry to Sweet across 5 levels.
tip.acidity: What you taste as sour is 'Acidity' — typically 6–10 g/L for whites, 5–7 g/L for reds. The salivation tells you the level.
tip.body: Body is the perceived weight in your mouth — driven by alcohol, extract and residual sugar. Compared to skim milk vs. whole milk.
tip.tannin: The drying sensation is 'Tannin' — polyphenols from grape skins/seeds. They round out with age.
tip.finish: Finish length is measured in 'Caudalies' (1 sec = 1 caudalie) at the Bordeaux School of Oenology.
